source_value: Mitochondrial impairment is the common hypothesis across the complications reviewed; coenzyme A discussed

claim: Basal ganglia particularly vulnerable; a crisis carries a risk of irreversible injury rather than always leaving it

claim: One anti-PEG positive participant had titres rise at least fourfold by the third dose, returning to baseline by month 12, with reactions on 11 of 43 doses
source_value: One participant positive for anti-PEG at baseline; titres increased at least fourfold in the predose sample for dose 3 (day 52), then gradually decreased and returned to baseline at month 12; experienced grade 1 or 2 IRRs during 11/43 (25.6%) doses; continued treatment and has not experienced IRRs for more than a year

claim: C3 is essentially unaltered through an acute decompensation, while 2-MC is among the strongest correlates of plasma ammonia during one

note: 3-HP is NOT in the unaltered list; it was measured and does correlate with ammonia. A marker that predicts the next event and one that tracks the current event need not be the same

claim: Free carnitine in plasma falls during acute decompensation in propionic acidemia, as a comparison between groups of samples rather than within patients
source_value: Table 2, free carnitine plasma, column header 'Median + SD [Min-Max] (N)': no AMD 38.9 SD 16.8 [7.0-93.3] n=56; AMD 22.0 SD 12.4 [8.0-70.1] n=25; Bonferroni-adjusted P = 0.0370, unpaired Mann-Whitney U. Confirmed in the Results text as a decrease in PA patients during AMD

source_value: Discussion: we advise to determine free carnitine concentrations to monitor whether carnitine supplementation is sufficient during AMD, as free carnitine is relatively decreased during AMD
note: An independent route to the same analyte the depletion model points at, which is why the discriminant is presented as a convergence rather than a proposal

claim: Urinary excretion of free carnitine is decreased in PA and MMA while excretion of short-chain acylcarnitines, mostly propionylcarnitine, is increased
source_value: Two PA and two MMA patients: low plasma free carnitine, increased short-chain acylcarnitines; urinary excretion of free carnitine decreased while excretion of short-chain acylcarnitines, mostly propionylcarnitine, increased. Total carnitine decreased in skeletal muscle

claim: Acylcarnitines inhibit, and are translocated by, the renal carnitine transporter, so they compete with free carnitine for recovery from the filtrate
source_value: Carnitine transporter solubilised from rat renal apical brush-border membrane and reconstituted into liposomes, corresponding very probably to OCTN2. note: In vitro and in rat. The identification with OCTN2 is the authors' own qualified one, and no patient measurement establishes that the recovered fraction falls with the metabolite. Section 5.5 states the limitation

source_value: Mean (SD) annualized MDE rates: age <=1 y 2.6 (2.7), >1 to <=2 y 2.4 (4.2), >12 to <=18 y 0.2 (0.4); early-onset PA 1.2 (1.8) vs late-onset 0.3 (0.4). Cohort-wide mean 1.0 (1.6), 49/50 (98.0%) reporting MDEs

claim: The documented direction runs from carnitine depletion to CoA unavailability to mitochondrial impairment, not the reverse
source_value: Single-patient case report (n=1, a 21-month-old girl with B12-unresponsive methylmalonic aciduria). Carnitine increased hippurate excretion, an index of intramitochondrial ATP and CoA availability, raised short-chain urinary acylcarnitines, and reduced methylmalonate and methylcitrate. Carnitine acts by removing propionyl groups, releasing CoA and restoring ATP
note: Added because a draft of Section 5.1 had drawn the arrow the other way, from mitochondrial impairment to degraded carnitine handling. Nothing in the paper now asserts that direction, and Model C no longer needs either. The sample size is n=1 and the text now says so; the source's opening sentence is a general statement about the disorder and does not license a plural claim

claim: The two published PK/PD models of this system use a different structure from (1): the population dose-selection model treats each marker as a turnover state with first-order loss, and the translational model puts the indirect response on the enzyme and makes the markers a direct saturating function of it
source_value: Gao: 'An indirect inhibition Kin model was used to describe the PD response of 3-HP and 2-MC.' Attarwala: 'PCC protein expression rate was modeled as a linear function of plasma PCCA/B mRNA concentration using a 2-compartment indirect response PD model with an empirical effect compartment' and 'PCC protein-mediated reduction of 2-MC, 3-HP, and C3/C2 ratios was modeled using a direct sigmoidal maximum inhibition (Imax) model'
note: Added so the note says how it relates to the prior art it already cites. The two differ from each other at the marker: Gao gives the marker its own turnover equation, Attarwala gives it an algebraic Imax in PCC protein, whose Table 1 carries E0, base, IC50 and a fixed Imax and no biomarker turnover constant at all. Neither is Michaelis-Menten in the marker, which is the point the paragraph makes. Recorded as drift rather than a match for the Gao half: 'whose loss is first order' is the definition of the model class the abstract names, and not something the abstract states, since it carries no PD equations and no biomarker parameters. Same standard as C02 and C03
